transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-14 11:30am PT / 14:30 ET
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Amit Patel (Redwood AE), Claire Romero (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Tidal), Devon King (Tidal), Priya Shah (Tidal)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete):
- Quickstart demo of hosted generation (chat + text). Showed sandbox, streaming behavior, param tuning (temperature, top_p), and retry/fallback patterns.
- Discussed enterprise concerns (latency, data residency, SOC2).
- Agreed to run POC micro-benchmark and share security docs.

Topics: sandbox walkthrough, streaming vs non-streaming, max_tokens and truncation, concurrency, backoff/retry strategies, canary fallbacks, cost controls (batching/caching), console metrics.

Transcript:
[00:00] Amit: alright, hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Amit from Redwood Inference, i'm here with Claire who will run the tech bits, um quick 1 minute agenda, show the hosted sandbox, streaming demo, parameter walkthrough, then fallbacks and retry patterns and lastly Q&A.
[00:18] Marta: sounds good, thanks Amit, we only got 60 minutes so we'll try to be efficient, i'm Marta, product lead, Devon's infra, Priya is ML, quick context: we're evaluating hosted first then dedicated if timing/latency dictates.
[00:31] Claire: hi all, yep, i'll jump into the console in a sec. just to call out, i'll intentionally show a few failure modes so you can see our fallbacks in action.
[00:45] Devon: also want to validate cost numbers and how streaming affects concurrency — we run many small chats at 300 rps at peak.
[00:52] Amit: perfect, ok Claire, take it away.
[01:00] Claire: pulling up the sandbox, link in chat -> https://console.redwood.ai/sandbox/TIDAL-demo (note: sample link)
[01:12] Claire: starting with a simple chat call (streaming enabled). prompt: "Summarize user session logs into action items" then we'll increment tokens.
[01:28] Claire: streaming chunk 1... chunk 2... you can see bytes arriving as SSE events. if a chunk stalls, client can re-open from last token id, or we provide resume token in the header.
[01:45] Priya: pause — that resume token, does it require sticky routing or it's stateless?
[01:50] Claire: good q — for hosted streaming we do stateless resume via sequence offsets. we keep KV-cache on the server side for active sessions but resume token ties to request id. not sticky to a GPU unless the request is still in-flight.
[02:10] Marta: ok. show us the param knobs you mentioned.
[02:16] Claire: yep, temperature, top_p, max_new_tokens, stop sequences, and streaming_chunk_size. also context_window and truncation strategy. i'll set temperature 0.2 to show more deterministic output, and then demo 0.8 for creative.
[02:37] [03:00] Claire: (0.2 run) response is concise. (0.2 -> deterministic, less hallucination but can be blunt)
[03:10] Devon: how do you recommend balancing latency and token cost at our scale? 300 rps is non-trivial.
[03:18] Amit: two levers, batching and kv/prefix cache. batching reduces per-token overhead but adds latency, so for small chats use smallest batch size and enable prefix cache to reuse repeated context. we also recommend quantized lower-cost variants for non-critical returns.
[03:39] Priya: can we force a fallback to a smaller model automatically on overload?
[03:43] Claire: yes — routing policies let you set thresholds (latency P95 or queue depth) to fallback to a cost-tier model. we also do automatic A/B style canary where we route a % to the alt model. if primary fails we do immediate failover with a grace token of partial output.
[04:02] Marta: and when you say "fails" is that GPU OOM, timeout, or rate limit?
[04:07] Claire: all of the above — timeouts, memory OOM, and when upstream device returns an error. we surface a standardized error code so client logic can decide to retry or accept the fallback.
[04:22] [04:35] Claire: i'll show an induced failure: i'm going to set throughput throttle low so the instance fails. watch the console trace for the job.
[04:45] Claire: triggering... now you see the trace: retry policy attempted 2 times with exponential backoff (250ms, 750ms), then fallback to smaller-gen model. note logs show failure reason "kernel_time_exceeded" which is our internal shorthand.
[05:10] Devon: those backoffs, are they configurable per-route?
[05:14] Claire: yes per-route and per-tenant. you can set retry attempts, base backoff, and jitter. we also provide suggested defaults tuned by workload history in the Optimize tab.
[05:26] Marta: can we get a breakdown of cost impact of retries? we worry about retries multiplying token cost.
[05:31] Amit: good point — retries do add cost. our console surfaces token-level cost per attempt. Optimize will flag high retry rates and recommend lower attempt count + larger initial backoff for ambiguous network errors. also caching avoids repeated recomputation.
[05:52] [06:10] Priya: does the hosted sandbox keep logs? data retention policy?
[06:16] Amit: by default sandbox logs are ephemeral. for production you can set retention windows, opt out of storing request content, or enable customer-managed KMS for payload encryption at rest. SOC2 report and privacy doc link will be shared.
[06:30] Priya: good. and about redwood dedicated/private if we need that later — what's the migration path?
[06:36] Claire: same API surface. you pin model versions and rolling deploys are handled by config. private/VPC just swaps the infra; we can provide an on-prem package for air-gapped.
[06:52] Marta: ok demo of streaming parameters complete. can we see a non-streaming run and how to handle partials?
[07:00] Claire: sure, switching to synchronous non-streaming, same prompt, larger max_new_tokens. you'll see a single response payload. if it times out client should check response code and then retrieve partial via the job-id endpoint. partials are kept for a short window.
[07:22] Devon: job-id endpoint — is that REST? websocket?
[07:26] Claire: REST polling; we recommend streaming for real-time. job-id is useful for batch/polled UX.
[07:35] [07:50] Claire: next, concurrency behavior: i'll simulate 250 concurrent small chats. console shows throughput, P50/P95 latency buckets, token/sec, and active batching. you can pin concurrency caps per-api-key.
[08:10] Marta: you mentioned prefix cache earlier — show a quick before/after.
[08:15] Claire: running with cache off – avg tokens-per-call 40, average latency 220ms. enable prefix cache and rerun same prefix, latency drops to 90ms and token cost per call reduced by 30% since we avoid regen of prompt embedding.
[08:35] Priya: is caching sensitive to context changes? like if user metadata changes do you bust cache?
[08:40] Claire: cache keys are computed from pinned prefixes + hashed metadata fields you opt into. you can set TTLs and tag invalidation rules from the console.
[08:56] [09:10] Devon: how does streaming interact with partial cache? if we resume mid-stream will cache help?
[09:15] Claire: yes, KV cache stores decoded k/v layers for decoder-only models; resume will benefit as long as the sequence offset aligns to a cached prefix. resume token indicates where to look up.
[09:30] Marta: ok security quick Q — SSO, SCIM, RBAC?
[09:35] Amit: we support SSO via SAML or OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC for routes + model access. audit logs show token-level events. we'll add SOC2 and integration docs in follow-up.
[09:53] [10:10] Claire: jumping to failure modes at the network layer. i will throttle the network to simulate transient failures and show retry heuristics.
[10:20] Claire: now you can see log: request 4571 got ECONNRESET; automatic client retry kicked in with exponential backoff configured at route level. after 3 attempts the request succeeded on 2nd attempt, so cost shows 2 attempts.
[10:38] Marta: in that case, can we have idempotency tokens so downstream duplicate calls are suppressed?
[10:44] Claire: yes we recommend idempotency keys for POST-style generation requests, we dedupe at the request-store layer for a short window.
[10:55] Priya: what's the recommended approach for deterministic outputs for evaluation?
[11:00] Amit: use temperature 0, fixed seed and a quantized model if needed; also pin model + model revision. we record model hashes in the job metadata so you can reproduce outputs.
[11:16] [11:40] Claire: demoing the Optimize tab — it surfaces batching suggestions, quantization candidates, and expected cost delta if you move to an int8 variant. it's a short list of recommended config changes with simulated impact.
[11:55] Devon: do you do automatic quantization or is that opt-in?
[11:59] Claire: it's opt-in after review; quantized model variants are curated by our applied ML team. the console will simulate quality delta vs cost savings.
[12:10] Marta: any built-in eval hooks for regressions?
[12:14] Claire: yes, you can upload prompt/eval suites; we run continuous evals on rollout and alert on regression thresholds; push-button rollback available.
[12:28] [12:50] Priya: what about rate-limiting? we have spikey production loads.
[12:55] Amit: rate-limits by API key with burst tokens; you can also send an explicit priority flag for internal high-priority traffic and reserve capacity on Dedicated.
[13:10] Claire: now a small demo of a canary rollout: we'll roll 10% of traffic to a new rev and intentionally inject a regression in the prompt set; console shows quality drop and automatic rollback kicks in after threshold.
[13:30] Marta: nice — can we tune the thresholds?
[13:34] Claire: fully tunable. you can set evaluation metric, severity threshold, and rollback window.
[13:42] [13:55] Devon: question on tail latency — P99 spikes at 2s for us is okay, but we want to make sure fallback doesn't bounce back and forth. any cool-down?
[14:03] Claire: yes we use a hysteresis/cooldown policy so once a route falls back it stays on fallback for a configurable cool-down period to avoid flapping.
[14:18] Marta: you mentioned custom routing policies earlier — can we set per-region routing so EU traffic stays in EU?
[14:24] Amit: yes region-aware routing, and you can pin models to regions for data residency. for private deployment we can host within your VPC.
[14:38] [14:55] Priya: security follow-up — do you support customer-managed KMS?
[14:59] Amit: yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations, envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key. docs will be shared.
[15:10] Claire: quick note: there is a small mis-transcription possibility in the console names — we might call our console tab "Optimize" or "Cost" in older UI, apologies if i click the wrong one.
[15:22] Marta: haha ok fair.
[15:28] [15:40] Amit: let's do a live micro-benchmark — Claire will run the 300 rps synthetic with sample prompts from Priya's earlier doc. we've got a prepared script.
[15:50] Claire: running now... results streaming in: throughput stable at 280 rps due to client-side ramp, P50 110ms, P95 420ms. enabling prefix cache... re-run... P95 drops to 180ms.
[16:12] Devon: these numbers look promising; what's the expected cost per 1M requests with these settings?
[16:18] Amit: ballpark estimate in the console for your profile ~ $X,XXX for 1M short chats (we'll send detailed tailored pricing). cost varies widely with model and retry rate.
[16:32] Priya: any limits on prompt size or conversation history?
[16:36] Claire: model context windows apply; for longer histories we do recency + important-message pins. you'll see truncation strategy options in the console.
[16:50] [17:05] Marta: ok let's capture the wrap-up and next steps.
[17:10] Amit: recap — showed hosted sandbox streaming/resume, parameter knobs, retries/backoff, caching, Optimize recommendations, and canary + rollback. agreed actions: will send SOC2, pricing, and schedule POC scoping. Claire will run micro-benchmark with the sample prompt set.
[17:28] Devon: timeline: our infra can start POC week of Jun 28, but we'd like scoping June 21.
[17:34] Amit: we'll propose June 21, 90-minute scoping, invite infra and security.
[17:40] Priya: i'll upload prompts and traffic profile by end of day Jun 16.
[17:45] Amit: perfect, i'll follow up with links and next steps. thanks everyone.
[17:52] Marta: thanks, that was good.
[17:55] [17:58] END
